Centre can step in on airfares in rare cases, say new rules
points: The Centre can directly intervene on ticket pricing in extraordinary situations under a new set of aviation rules that also require airlines to disclose cancellation charges and refund conditions separately while displaying airfares to passengers.
These rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2024, were notified by the civil aviation ministry (MoCA) on October 26 and published in the Gazette of India on October 31.
They will come into effect on January 1, 2027, replacing the Aircraft Rules, 1937.
The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, which replaced the Aircraft Act, 1934, came into force on January 1, 2025.
The new rules shift the intervention power on specified tariff-related grounds from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) to the Central Government.
Under Rule 135(4) of the Aircraft Rules, 1937, the DGCA could issue directions to an airline if it was satisfied that the airline was charging excessive tariff.
The new provisions build on disclosure requirements that already existed under the Aircraft Rules, 1937.

items.title: FPIs are buying again. Why is their share of Indian stocks still falling?
points: Foreign investors’ ownership of Indian equities has fallen to its lowest level in nearly 15 years amid valuation concerns, geopolitical uncertainty, and elevated US bond yields, even as they returned to the market as net buyers in the September quarter.

A Mint analysis of 5,638 BSE-listed companies sourced from the CMIE database showed that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) held 14.02% of shares at the end of the September quarter (Q2FY27), their lowest since December 2011.
It is now 6.07 percentage points below its December 2020 peak of 20.09%, reflecting a sustained retreat by overseas investors.
FPIs, however, turned net buyers during the September quarter, net investing ₹13,970 crore.
In the final week of October, FPIs bought stocks worth more than ₹14,000 crore.
Their ownership rose to 11.59% in September from 11.50% in June and 10.79% a year earlier.
Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) invested a net ₹1.7 trillion in Indian equities during the September quarter, compared with net inflows of ₹13,970 crore from FPIs.

items.title: North Korea Denies Role in $6.3 Billion Binance Crypto Heist
points: North Korea rejected US claims that it was behind the theft of more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, after the FBI blamed Pyongyang for the biggest crypto heist on record.

The US assertion that North Korea is responsible for the Binance attack is “absurd rhetoric and nothing new,” Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, said in a statement carried by the official Korean Central News Agency Tuesday.

“It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads the international public opinion as if all the cyber crimes in different parts of the world are our deeds,” the statement said, referring to North Korea by its official name.
The rebuttal came after the FBI said Saturday that North Korea was behind the theft of more than $6 billion in virtual assets from Binance on or around Oct.
The agency identified the operation as being linked to TradeTraitor, a North Korea hacking campaign previously linked to cryptocurrency thefts.

items.title: China Boosts Use of Stock Support Tools to Stabilize Market
points: China will encourage financial institutions to make fuller use of two stock support tools and optimize their terms, as authorities step up efforts to bolster market stability and confidence.

Separately, it will cut the rate on its relending facility for share buybacks and stake increases to 1% from 1.25%, make the program permanent and encourage banks to increase lending, the PBOC said.
The two tools were introduced in October 2024 as Beijing sought to shore up the stock market.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission said in a separate statement that a third round of swap operations will begin in coming days, with 31 securities and fund firms approved to participate and applying for more than 100 billion yuan of quotas.

items.title: Despite court rulings, people continue to face difficulty in CID clearance: M.Y. Tarigami
points: CPI(M) leader and lawmaker Mohammad Yousuf Tarigami.
Tarigami on Monday said that despite court rulings, many people continue to face difficulties in getting Criminal Investigation Department (CID) clearance in Kashmir.
“The High Court has, in several cases, ruled that a person cannot be denied security clearance simply because of the alleged involvement of their relatives in militancy-related activities.

However, despite these court rulings, many people continue to face difficulties in getting CID clearance because of the alleged involvement of even distant relatives in such activities,” said Mr. Tarigami.
He said that in some cases, those accused died many years ago, but their past continues to affect their families, denying the younger generations opportunities through no fault of their own.
“The verification process needs to be reviewed to ensure that individuals are assessed on the basis of their own conduct, not the alleged actions of their relatives.
Security concerns are important, but they should not come at the cost of the rights and future of innocent people,” he added.

This policy brief looks at the investment dimension of the ETS proposal with respect to the aviation and maritime sectors.
They are major contributors to the ETS revenue generation.
We argue, however, that the proposed framework is not fit for purpose to adequately support clean fuel investments in these hard-to-abate sectors.
The ETS Review is an opportunity to set up a tailor-made investment tool to de-risk and boost the production and uptake of e-fuels, using the ETS funds from aviation and shipping.

Early financial support is crucial for the development of a domestic e-fuels value chain, Europe’s geostrategic autonomy and the EU’s industrial position in the global competition for clean technologies.
Source: European Federation for Transport and Environment

items.title: PortXchange says measuring emissions isn’t enough
points: Ports have spent years improving how they calculate and report emissions.
That frustration has emerged repeatedly in PortXchange’s conversations with ports seeking better ways to manage their environmental impact.
They want to understand emissions across their operations, anticipate future changes and assess the consequences of major investments.

PortXchange is responding by expanding EmissionInsider, with new features coming to the platform including multimodal emissions monitoring, emissions forecasting, scenario modelling and AI-assisted decarbonisation planning.
Sjoerd de Jager, Managing Director & Co-Founder of PortXchange, believes the industry has spent too long treating emissions reporting as the end of the process rather than the starting point.
“Ports have become much better at measuring emissions, but measuring them doesn’t make them disappear,” de Jager said.

PortXchange is developing EmissionInsider’s multimodal capabilities to bring these sources together, giving ports a clearer view of which activities drive most emissions and where reductions are possible.
The expanded platform is being organised around four connected products: Emission Report, Emission Dashboard, Emission Simulations and Emission Strategy.

items.title: Seafarers Hospital Society develops new KPIs to strengthen medical emergency preparedness and response at sea
points: New emergency-focused health indicators build on SHS’s Best Practice KPI framework, helping maritime operators measure readiness, response, outcomes and learning when medical emergencies occur onboard.

The Seafarers Hospital Society (SHS) has developed a dedicated set of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) surrounding medical emergencies onboard, expanding its wider Best Practice KPI work to address the specific challenges of responding to serious illness…
The KPIs provide a structured approach to assess how effectively maritime organisations prepare for, respond to and learn from medical emergencies.

Their development follows an extensive workshop in June, convened by SHS alongside medical experts from the International Maritime Health Association (IMHA) and International Maritime Health Foundation (IMHF) in response to emerging threats facing…

Dr Nebojša Nikolić, President of the Management Board at the IMHF, said: “From our perspective these KPIs provide a structured approach to measuring preparedness, response and recovery from medical emergencies at sea.

items.title: NAVTOR redefines real-time fleet monitoring with AIS streaming in NavFleet
points: NAVTOR is steering fleet monitoring and management towards new horizons with the introduction of AIS streaming to the NavFleet platform.

In doing so, the Norwegian-headquartered company is “inventing something unique” – using its own digital ecosystem to capture live vessel AIS data so management teams can see exactly where ships are, and what they’re doing, in real-time.
Or, as NAVTOR describes it, “in real-real-time”.
The latest release of NavFleet, version 2.7.1, is a landmark upgrade.
The AIS development, says Tor Håkon Svanes, NAVTOR’s NavFleet Platform Manager, takes centre stage.
As the world’s leading maritime technology company, NAVTOR supplies products and services to over 18,000 vessels in the world fleet.

NavFleet 2.7.1 – users now have the ability to zoom in on any vessel, anywhere, delivering new levels of operational insight and awareness Svanes reveals that an upcoming release of NavFleet will also offer users the ability to ‘replay’ streams to see not…

items.title: Alternative fuels comprised 12% of NYK’s marine fuel mix in 2025
points: Low greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions marine fuels accounted for 12.2% of Japanese shipping company NYK Line’s total fuel consumption in the financial year 2025 (FY2025).
Japanese shipping company Nippon Yusen Kabushiki Kaisha (NYK Line) continued to expand its dual-fuel fleet, operating 35 such vessels in the previous financial year, up from 26 in 2024.
Biofuels comprised the largest share of NYK Line’s marine fuel mix during the mentioned period, followed by LNG.

The shipping company is actively “increasing the use of biofuels and alternative fuels available today to achieve immediate GHG emissions reductions.” NYK Line’s progressive shift toward low-emission marine fuels helped the company to reduce its emissions…

Biofuel usage cut emissions by an estimated 200,000 mt CO2e relative to energy-equivalent heavy fuel oil like HSFO, NYK Line said, adding that the emissions reductions were verified by ISCC certification.
The shipping company laid a groundwork for broader biofuel adoption with the launch of a 12-month B100 (100% biofuel) pilot project aboard a car carrier in May 2026.

items.title: OneLearn Global and RINA unite technical training and seafarer wellbeing in new learning partnership
points: OneLearn Global (OLG),a member of OneCare Group, and RINA have joined forces to deliver an integrated maritime learning offering that brings together technical competence, digital learning, human performance and seafarer wellbeing.

Through this collaboration, the two organisations will expand access to high-quality education designed to strengthen professional competence, human performance and workforce resilience across the maritime sector.

Under the collaboration, selected courses from the RINA Learning Hub will be made available through the OLG Learning Experience Platform (LXP), while selected OLG courses will be offered through the RINA Learning Hub.
The initial rollout will focus on Greece and Singapore, with the potential to expand into additional markets.

By combining RINA’s technical maritime expertise with OLG’s digital learning capabilities and OneCare Group’s expertise in seafarer wellbeing, the collaboration aims to provide maritime organisations with a more holistic approach to workforce development.
Marinos Kokkinis, CEO of OneCare Group, said: “The maritime workforce of the future will need more than technical competence alone.

items.title: MacGregor: Record profitability and strong order intake across all divisions – delivering on the Full Ahead strategy
points: MacGregor’s Q3 performance • MacGregor’s third quarter 2026 was characterised by strong order intake in all divisions and record profitability.
MacGregor’s Q1 to Q3 performance • MacGregor delivered strong order intake, continued profitability expansion and strong cash conversion during the period 1 January to 30 September 2026.

MacGregor CEO Jonas Gustavsson: ”In the third quarter of 2026, our orders received totalled EUR 305.4 million, representing an increase of 126 percent year-on-year, supported by strong sales execution and continued high demand.
The strong order intake was broad-based across all divisions.
The high order intake further strengthened our order book, which reached EUR 1,337 million at the end of Q3 2026, providing continued good visibility for the years ahead.
In Merchant, sales decreased by 8 percent, primarily due to the timing of customer deliveries, while sales in Offshore clearly increased.
We remain fully committed to executing our Full Ahead strategy.” In the third quarter 2026 interim report, MacGregor restates certain periodic figures for the third and fourth quarter of 2025.

items.title: Türkiye Strengthens Demand For Steelpaint’s Long-Term Corrosion Protection
points: The rise in the number of Turkish shipyards from 37 in 2002 to about 85 today has substantially increased the country’s newbuild capacity but shiprepair and maintenance continues to account for much of the industry’s maritime activity, as more shipowners…
For instance, Turkish yards, concentrated around the Tuzla, Yalova and Kocaeli regions, repaired or maintained 46.4 million dwt in 2024, compared with 13.1 million dwt in 2011.
And although 2025 throughput eased to 42.4 million dwt, long-term projections reflect a strong position in the international repair market.

“Shipowners are looking much more closely at the cost of maintaining their vessels over their remaining service lives and coating quality is increasingly seen as a way of reducing the maintenance spend over the long term,” says Steelpaint director Frank…

Türkiye’s newbuilding industry is also providing new opportunities for Steelpaint’s range of single-component, moisture-cured polyurethane coatings, particularly Stelpant PU-Zinc and PU-Combination 300.

items.title: Treasury Yields Extend Past Month’s Slide as Oil Prices Drop
points: (Bloomberg) -- Treasuries rose, building on their biggest monthly advance in more than two years, as tumbling oil prices eased concern about inflation pressure leading to additional Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes.
Ten- to 30-year maturities led gains, with yields for those tenors declining about four basis points to touch the lowest levels since September.
Equities weakness concentrated in large technology company shares benefited the Treasury market last month as investors piled into lower-risk assets.

“The historical negative correlation between bonds and equities seems to have returned over the past month, and the gains today could be related to investors looking to protect further downside in equities,” said Steven Zeng, an interest-rate strategist at…
The oil price slide “also supports Treasury yields to move lower.” The US 10-year yield declined as much as six basis points to under 4.87%, the lowest level since Sept.

items.title: Cyclonic storm Murasu to make landfall close to Ongole
points: A satellite image of Cyclone Murasu over the Bay of Bengal on Sunday.

IMD | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement As the cyclonic storm, Cyclone Murasu, moves towards the A.P. coast, the State has deployed six National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and seven State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams in districts likely…

State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA), the landfall point is likely to be Ongole and in this connection, two teams each have been stationed in the districts of Krishna, Bapatla, Guntur, Nellore and Prakasam, while one team each has been deployed in…
According to the 9 p.m. bulletin from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the cyclonic storm centred over Southwest and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal at 5.30 p.m.

It was located about 420 km east-southeast of Chennai, 490 km east-southeast of Nellore, 500 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 510 east-southeast of Kavali, 530 km southeast of Ongole and 560 km south-southeast of Vishakhapatnam.

items.title: Alternative-Fuel Ship Orders Outpace Port Bunkering Infrastructure, Lloyd’s Register Warns
points: Photo credit: Port of Rotterdam The global shipping industry is ordering alternative-fuel vessels faster than ports can develop the infrastructure needed to fuel them, according to a new report from Lloyd’s Register (LR), highlighting a growing challenge…

LR’s new Fuel for Thought: Ports report, released Monday, found that 1,942 alternative-fuel-capable vessels were on order as of January 2026, representing 47% of the global orderbook by tonnage, according to Clarksons Research.
Commercial ammonia bunkering, meanwhile, has been recorded at only one port, following the first operation at Ulsan, South Korea, in April 2026.

As gCaptain reported in October, data from DNV’s Alternative Fuels Insight platform showed that shipowners ordered 69 alternative-fuel vessels in September, the highest monthly total in nearly two years.
The surge brought alternative-fuel orders to 311 vessels through the first nine months of 2026, up 53% from the same period a year earlier.

items.title: Hanwha Philly Shipyard Names New President as U.S. Navy Expansion Accelerates
points: National Security Multi-Mission Vessels (NSMV) under construction at Hanwha Philly Shipyard.

Photo courtesy Hanwha Philly Shipyard Hanwha Philly Shipyard has named shipbuilding veteran Hyuk Kim as its new president, effective November 2, as the Philadelphia yard moves ahead with plans to expand into U.S. Navy shipbuilding while maintaining its…

Kim, who brings more than 25 years of naval and commercial shipbuilding experience, succeeds David Kim, who helped oversee Hanwha’s acquisition of the shipyard in 2024 and a near doubling of its workforce since then.
The appointment follows a series of major developments at the yard, including last week’s selection of HDUSA to build a $269 million Medium Landing Ship for the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps.

“Hanwha’s upgrades and investments in Philly Shipyard are enabling the yard to now build for the federal government as well as commercial ships, bringing the Philadelphia waterfront back to its roots as a key part of the Arsenal of Democracy,” Anderson said.

items.title: ‘India’s green-energy shift shielded it from global crises’: Prime Minister Narendra Modi
points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday said India’s decade-long shift to renewable energy had helped the country sustain high economic growth despite global disruptions, including the Covid-19 pandemic and the West Asia crisis.

Inaugurating the Bharat Renewable Energy (BRE) Summit & Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, Modi warned that continued over-reliance on fossil fuels would repeatedly disrupt the global economy.
But 140 crore (1,400 million) Indians take pride in how effectively the nation has managed the turmoil while maintaining high economic growth,” Modi said in his inaugural address.
India now ranks among the top three nations in solar and renewable energy, with over 50% non-fossil installed capacity and nearly 300 GW already achieved towards the 500 GW target,” Modi said.
“For Africa, a proposal for a $200 million Africa Solar Facility has also been put forward,” he said, adding that the coming decade was vital for global climate goals.

items.title: A month after RBI’s rate hike, banks start raising deposit rates as liquidity shrinks, Bank of India the latest to move
points: Domestic banks are beginning to increase their deposit rates due to shrinking liquidity conditions in the market.
Bank of India recently announced a rate hike on deposits for various maturities, including a special 500-day option.
This decision reflects the growing cost of deposits in the banking system as demand for credit rises.
Banking system liquidity has significantly decreased from its peak in early September.

items.title: Queues and chaos at many Tasmac outlets as ₹10 price hike, fake news of closure of shops
points: A Tasmac outlet in Koyambedu witnessed long queues as fake news of uncertainty over the functioning of liquor outlets spread all over social media on Monday. | Photo Credit: B.

VELANKANNI RAJ Despite the rain on Monday, hundreds of tipplers stood in queue for hours at Tasmac outlets across Chennai and neighbouring districts, fearing that more liquor shops could down their shutters.
On Sunday, many Tasmac shops pulled shutters down without informing the management.

The reason: Tasmac had said last week that it will increase the maximum retail price (MRP) of all liquor variants in the State by ₹10 with effect from November 1 by adding an environment cess to the existing price.
And tipplers can get this ₹10 reimbursed by returning the empty liquor bottles.
Tasmac also suspended its workers across Tamil Nadu who were responsible for the shop closure on Sunday and Monday.
As on July 2026, Tasmac has 4,048 retail vending shops and a workforce of 22,877 (6,473 supervisors, 14,379 salespersons, and 2,025 assistant salespersons).
